decisions.executionNote: Begin left-arm elbow-up approach toward the coin in the left workspace; bank is on the right. Keep both grippers open.
Advance the left wrist above the holder while progressively turning the fingers downward; maintain elbow-up continuity.
Approach above the left coin and rotate toward a vertical pinch matching its visible plane. The remaining alignment will use the wrist view.
Bring the open left fingers above the holder with a near-downward approach. Slow final alignment follows.
Fine-align the left pinch to the coin seen right of center in the wrist image; finish the downward orientation before closing.
Center the coin between the left fingertips, lower a few millimeters, and begin a slow pinch while checking the wrist image.
Finish closing the left fingers on the coin at holder height. Retention remains uncertain until a short vertical lift is observed.
Lift the closed left gripper vertically to check that the coin separates from the holder; keep the right arm parked.
Continue the vertical lift past 8 cm and inspect separation from the holder before transferring the coin.
The coin remains visibly in the holder, so reopen and return for a corrected pinch, shifting slightly across the coin plane.
Coin is now laterally centered. Lower the open pinch to overlap more of its upper rim, then partially close for a visual alignment check.
Close and settle the centered pinch without moving the wrist, then verify retention with a short lift.
Test the corrected grasp with a gentle vertical lift, keeping the pinch fully closed and watching coin-holder separation.
Continue a short closed-gripper lift to distinguish a retained coin from one still resting in the holder.
Coin is not retained. Reopen and descend for a lower, more precise pinch rather than attempting a transfer.
Lower the pinch farther onto the coin and slightly match its plane; previous centered attempts did not retain it.
Match the coin plane more closely while completing a lower pinch; use a small upward correction to keep the rim within the jaws.
Settle the fully closed lower pinch, then test with a 15 mm lift while watching whether the coin moves with the fingertips.
Adjust the pinch longitudinally along the coin plane; the preceding lift did not show clear retention. Reopen before shifting, then close gently.
Settle the shifted pinch fully closed and make a short lift to test retention from the wrist image.
Lift another 3 cm with the pinch closed and inspect whether the gold coin stays at the fingertip rather than in the holder.
The coin has tilted out of the pinch. Reopen and observe its settled position before making another grasp.
The coin has fallen beside the holder. Approach its new visible position from above with open fingers for a rim pinch.
Visually center the flat coin beneath the open fingers, using small downward and lateral corrections.
Center the flat coin across the jaws and lower to its rim, beginning a gradual closure only after the lateral correction.
Close around the centered flat coin at the current contact height without pushing farther into the tabletop.
Test the rim grasp by lifting vertically with the left gripper fully closed; inspect the coin against the stationary holder.
The coin now stays between the left jaws while the holder recedes. Lift clear and begin preparing the right arm for a central handoff.
Maintain the retained rim grasp while slowly turning the coin upright and moving toward a central handoff; right fingers remain open.
Continue the slow, separated approach to a central handoff, holding the coin securely while turning its face upright.
Raise the coin's face toward vertical while keeping it on the left side; stage the right gripper short of contact for a face pinch.
Continue orienting the retained coin upright at the center boundary. The right arm approaches without closing or crossing the left wrist.
Finish turning the coin upright and stage the open right gripper beside its exposed upper rim for handoff.
Replan with smaller left-wrist increments after the continuity rejection; finish alignment without forcing the unexecuted motion.
Hold the upright coin still with the left arm and advance the open right fingers toward its exposed rim, using wrist alignment.
The perpendicular grippers appear to contact near the coin edge. Raise the right pinch toward the exposed upper rim before any further closure.
Narrow the right gripper and approach the exposed upper edge in small increments, leaving the left grasp closed until transfer is verified.
Advance the right pinch the remaining short distance toward the coin's upper rim, keeping the donor grasp closed and monitoring clearance.
Lower the right fingertips slightly onto the visible upper rim and close, while the left arm continues supporting the coin.
The right pinch appears tangent to the coin. Reopen slightly and place it a few millimeters farther over the upper face before reclosing.
Relieve donor-jaw interference slowly while seating and closing the right pinch on the upper coin rim. Verify transfer before withdrawing farther.
The coin fell during handoff. Separate the arms and reopen, preparing a right-side approach to its settled position near the center.
Replan the rejected clearing motion with smaller rotations and translations; no part of the previous chunk executed.
Withdraw the empty left arm and shape a slow angled right approach to the coin near the workspace boundary, preserving elbow-up continuity.
Clear the left arm further and lower the open right gripper along an angled approach toward the visible coin, slowing before table contact.
Continue the angled right approach toward the flat coin while retracting the empty left arm toward home; keep the fingers open above the table.
Align the right jaws laterally with the coin and descend toward its rim on the angled approach. Finish returning the left arm close to its origin.
Seat the angled right pinch farther onto the coin rim with small lateral corrections, while completing the left arm's return to origin.
Close the right jaws around the now-centered coin rim without further tableward motion; then inspect retention on a lift.
The coin slid ahead rather than being retained. Reopen, move the angled pinch farther over its center, and retry without pressing into the table.
Close around the centered coin rim and begin a very short lift to test the corrected right-hand grasp.
The coin shifted to the right of the pinch. Reopen and recenter across its rim with a very small height correction before closing again.
Close on the centered rim, settle, and test with a short vertical lift. Keep the left arm parked.
Lift and draw the closed right pinch clear toward its own workspace, checking whether the coin remains fixed relative to the fingers.
The coin remains on the table. Clear the right arm and bring the left arm toward the coin to reposition it into the right workspace for a more vertical pickup.
Prepare an angled left-side approach behind the flat coin, keeping the right arm clear and both elbow-up configurations continuous.
Continue the left approach behind the coin, gradually aiming the fingers toward its rim while keeping clear of the tabletop and parked right arm.
Bring the angled left fingers just behind the coin, finishing orientation before a gentle rightward repositioning.
Set the closed left fingertips behind the coin's near rim at table height, preparing a small rightward slide into an easier pickup area.
Gently slide the coin rightward with the low left fingertips while the right arm stays clear above the table; inspect motion before continuing.
Continue the controlled tabletop slide toward the center boundary. Keep the right arm elevated and the left wrist on its own side.
Finish the short tabletop repositioning with a slight lateral correction, leaving the coin reachable by a vertical right-hand pickup.
